newsitem.title: UK: Moody's confirms Endesa notes at AA2.
newsitem.headline: Moody's confirms Endesa notes at AA2.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Ltd said on Monday it confirmed the AA2 debt ratings of International Endesa B.V.'s $750 million Euro-medium-term-note programme, euronotes and Swiss notes.
This entity is fully guaranteed by Empresa Nacional de Electricidad S.A. (ENDESA).

"This rating action follows the announcement that Endesa had made a public offer to acquire up to 75 percent of the shares of both Compania Sevillana de Electricidad S.A. (Sevillana) and Fuerzas Electricas de Cataluna S.A. (FECSA) for an amount of approximately 200,000 million pesatas," Moody's said in a statement.

"The confirmation reflects Moody's expectation that stronger cash flow, fueled by supportive regulation, recovery in demand, cost containment, and moderate investments in diversification together with lower capital expenditure needs, will continue to enable ENDESA to improve its debt-protection measurements over the intermediate term," Moody's said.

In addition, Moody's ratings of ENDESA had previously considered that it was exposed to both the operating strengths and financial weaknesses of the two Spanish utilities through its existing 39.5 percent equity stake in Sevillana and 48.9 percent stake in FECSA.

"In spite of the magnitude of this transaction and the fact that it will be debt financed, Moody's expects that ENDESA will strengthen its competitive position by consolidating its balanced mix of generation and distribution facilities," Moody's said.

The financial risk represented by these investments should diminish over time, as the financial performance of the utilities gradually improves, Moody's said. ENDESA group ranks among the four largest European electric utilities. ENDESA's installed electricity generating capacity of some 21,847 mw, represents about 54 percent of the total installed capacity in Spain.
